author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Russian attacks on two petrol stations in Kyiv killed two people early Friday, Mayor Vitali Klitschko said. Eight others were injured at the fuel sites, and emergency services said a rescue worker was among those hurt when one location was struck again.

The attacks followed an overnight strike on a residential block in the capital that injured eight people. A woman was also killed in the region surrounding Kyiv, according to the regional governor. Russia has resumed frequent waves of jet-powered drone attacks on the capital and its suburbs after a short pause during a visit by U.S. peace envoys.

Ukraine also carried out overnight strikes inside Russia. Officials said a drone attack killed two people in the Tula region, while Ukrainian forces targeted logistics and other economic sites, including an Ozon distribution hub in the Saratov region.

Both sides have increasingly focused on fuel, transport and logistics infrastructure as the war moves toward another winter. Casualty figures and damage assessments can change as emergency crews search affected sites. The renewed attacks show that diplomatic contacts have not stopped the expanding campaign against economic targets and nearby civilian areas.
dek: Eight people were injured at two fuel sites as Russia and Ukraine continued attacks on logistics and economic targets overnight.
headline: Russian strikes on Kyiv petrol stations kill two, officials say
